P.text: addOrderToBook() calls _updateBookPostOrder, which adds the order to storage, and then calls _updateLimitPostOrder with the order passed as type memory
P.evidence_quote:
after the `order` has already been added to storage in _updateBookPostOrder.
_updateLimitPostOrder is called, and the order passed into _updateLimitPostOrder is of type `memory`

I.text: updates to the order's prevOrderId in _updateLimitPostOrder must be reflected in the stored order so the book remains orderly
I.evidence_quote: when the `prevOrderId` for the new order is updated, this only happens to the order passed in and not the one in storage.

V.text: orders added to the book do not have their prevOrderId saved, disrupting orderliness and causing orders to become lost and unfillable; removal treats such an order as head, leaving earlier orders lost
V.evidence_quote:
all the orders added to the book do not have their `prevOrderId` saved with them.
This will severely disrupt the orderliness of the book, leading to orders becoming lost in the book and can never be filled.
